key_insight: A generalized lattice Boltzmann framework can simulate Navier-Stokes flows on continuously varying orthogonal grids by embedding metric-aware equilibrium and forcing terms into the collide-and-stream algorithm.
engineering_relevance: This enables efficient boundary-layer and multiscale flow simulations with local grid clustering while preserving LBM simplicity and compatibility with complex coordinate systems.
method: Use a coordinate transformation to express the flow equations in general orthogonal coordinates.
Derive equilibrium moments and geometric forcing terms via Chapman-Enskog analysis using local metric factors and their derivatives.
Implement the model with modular collision operators; the central-moments MRT variant is reported as the most robust.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on multiple benchmark flow problems and two case studies, including efficient boundary-layer and MHD coupled simulations on orthogonal curvilinear grids.
watch_item: Accurate implementation requires careful handling of metric derivatives and correction terms, so the method may be sensitive to discretization and coordinate-generation details.
paper_title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Navier-Stokes Equations in General Orthogonal Coordinates for Efficient Flow Simulations using Nonuniform Clustered Grids
